page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a cloud server instance within the High Performance family, provisioned with 4 shared virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration features simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware AES encryption and BMI2. The instance includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, 180 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects mid-tier single-threaded output and constrained multi-threaded scaling. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput reached 1456.98 points (mid-range), while multi-core performance measured 5760.92 points, falling into the bottom quartile. Geekbench scores display a similar pattern, registering 1182.0 in single-core tasks and 3820.0 in multi-core routines. Memory testing demonstrates 409.04 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 36.98 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 29.37 GB/sec for writes. The PassMark CPU score settled at 6534.67, with database operations scoring 1350.89 and PassMark memory rating at 1722.49. In workload-specific benchmarks, Clang compilation reached 5780.0 points, Redis achieved 6.27 million SET operations per second, and static web serving delivered 6.27 GB/sec throughput.

Due to its shared CPU allocation model and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this configuration provides cost-efficient entry-level compute resources without dedicating full physical cores. The included 180 GB local NVMe SSD offers high-speed local disk capacity without requiring supplemental block storage attachments. The instance is suited for lightweight build steps, development environments, staging servers, single-threaded batch processing, and non-critical web serving.

This server is appropriate for lightweight continuous integration tasks, web staging environments, internal caching services, and low-concurrency general application hosting.
